item.title: Imperatives at a craft table
item.explanation_text:
Use an imperative to tell someone what to do. Use the base form of the verb in an affirmative imperative, like cut, sort, or wash. Say “Cut the paper in half.” The person you are speaking to knows the instruction is for them, so you usually leave out you.

To tell someone what to avoid, put don’t before the base verb. Say “Don’t cut the blue paper.” You can also use do not, which you often see on signs. A common mistake is to write “Don’t to cut.” After don’t or do not, use cut without to.

You can add please to make an instruction sound more polite. Put it at the start in “Please wash the cups” or at the end in “Wash the cups, please.” It also works in a negative instruction, as in “Please don’t use the big scissors.” When the craft table is closing, use an imperative to tell people where to put things back.
item.contrast_text: “You wash the brushes” can describe what someone usually does. “Wash the brushes” gives that person an instruction.
item.common_error_pattern: Learners sometimes put to after don’t or do not. Use “Don’t open the glue” instead of “Don’t to open the glue.”

examples.bad: To cut the card in half.
Please sorts the buttons by color.
examples.good: Please sort the buttons by color.

examples.bad: Please not put wet brushes in the box.
examples.good: Please don't put wet brushes in the box.

children.title: Put the lids back on
children.instructions: Put the tiles in order to make an instruction. Use every tile once. Keep the comma and the period attached to their words.
children.prompt_text: the lids / jars, / on / Put / please. / the
accepted_answers: Put the lids on the jars, please.

children.title: Protect the paper shapes
children.instructions: Change the sentence into a negative imperative. Start with Please, then use don't or do not. Keep the rest of the sentence.
accepted_answers: Please don't touch the wet paper shapes.
Please do not touch the wet paper shapes.

children.title: Close the craft table
children.instructions: Tell a visitor what to do. Change the sentence into an affirmative imperative. Start with Put, keep the words after put, and end with a comma and please.
children.prompt_text: The craft table is closing. You put the glue sticks back in the drawer.
accepted_answers: Put the glue sticks back in the drawer, please.
